cases.prompt: A high-impedance microelectrode records a smaller signal after connecting a digitizer. Explain loading with a divider model and give two circuit or measurement changes that test whether the loss is electrical rather than biological.

rubric.criterion: Models electrode/source impedance in series with finite input impedance
Predicts attenuation from the divider
Suggests higher input impedance, buffer amplifier, impedance sweep, or dummy-signal control

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 1 (suggested week 13). Compute the resonant angular frequency of the candidates and convert it to hertz (project task 1).

rubric.criterion: I computed ω₀ from L and C alone, and did not use R in the resonance condition.
I converted to cycles per second by dividing by 2π, and labeled the two results with their units.
I checked that the frequency is shared by all three candidates and explained why R does not move it.

limitations: This project milestone self-check is not collected or scored; it is not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 2 (suggested week 13). Compute Q, bandwidth, both half-power frequencies and the peak and RMS currents, and state what changes when only R changes (project task 2).

rubric.criterion: I computed Q = ω₀L/R and Δω = R/L from the declared components.
I found both half-power frequencies and checked that they differ by the bandwidth and multiply to ω₀².
I distinguished peak from RMS current and identified which quantities R alone changes.

limitations: This project milestone self-check is not collected or scored; it is not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 3 (suggested week 13). Compute the average resistor power at resonance and compare the maximum magnetic and electric stored energies (project task 3).

rubric.criterion: I used the RMS current for the average power and explained why the peak value would be wrong.
I computed both ½LI_peak² and ½CV²_C,peak and showed they are equal here.
I explained why the two maxima need not occur at the same instant.

limitations: This project milestone self-check is not collected or scored; it is not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 4 (suggested week 14). Apply all three selection limits and identify the surviving candidate and each rejection's binding failure (project task 4).

rubric.criterion: I evaluated Q, bandwidth and peak current against all three stated limits.
I named the candidate that meets every limit.
I identified the single binding failure for each rejected candidate instead of listing all of its values.

limitations: This project milestone self-check is not collected or scored; it is not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 5 (suggested week 14). Compute the impedance magnitude, current peak and phase at the stated off-resonance frequency, and identify lead or lag from the sign of the net reactance (project task 5).

rubric.criterion: I combined ωL and 1/(ωC) into a signed net reactance.
I computed |Z|, the current peak and the phase angle under the exp(jωt) convention.
I used the sign of the net reactance, not intuition, to decide lead versus lag.

limitations: This project milestone self-check is not collected or scored; it is not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Series-resonance project milestone 6 (suggested week 14). State which parts of the calculation depend on ideal linear components and what an observed resonance curve alone cannot establish (project task 6).

rubric.criterion: I identified which formulas assume constant, linear R, L and C.
I described what a measured curve cannot distinguish, such as where the loss actually sits.
I kept the conclusion inside the synthetic, single-mesh model without device or biological claims.
